correctness.rationale: The symbol θ=e^{iaz} has bounded derivatives (ia)^k θ, so Leibniz shows Mθ bounded on the derivative-defined H_n^p for 1<=p<=∞. For |λ|>1, θ-λ and all derivatives of 1/(θ-λ) are bounded on C+, yielding a bounded inverse multiplier. For 0<|λ|<1, zeros z_k=(arg λ+2πk)/a+i(-log|λ|)/a lie at infinite distinct interior points; each evaluation functional is continuous and finite collections are linearly independent via rational interpolation P(z)/(z+i)^{N+n+1}, hence the range has infinite codimension and cannot be Fredholm. For |λ|=1, take x with θ(x)=λ and normalized Fε=cε/(z-x+iε)^2; boundary scaling fixes ||Fε^(n)||_p=1 with cε ~ ε^{n+2-1/p} (or ε^{n+2} for p=∞). Leibniz and |θ(t)-λ|<=min(2,a|t-x|) yield ||(θ-λ)Fε||_{H_n^p}→0; p=1 logarithm multiplied by ε power also vanishes. An injective Fredholm operator is bounded below, contradiction. Closure gives λ=0. Independent finite rational interpolation and boundary-scaling checks corroborate proof, not replace the Banach argument.
